writeup.headline: Azenta rates Hold: a debt-free balance sheet and strong price trend offset weak margins and a high valuation.
writeup.thesis: Azenta scores 56, a Hold, 9 points short of Buy and 12 points above Sell. The balance sheet scores 100 because the company has net cash and no debt. The trend scores 87, with the price 43.3% above its 200-day average, shares 66.6 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, and the price 4.9% below its 52-week high. Growth scores 63 on latest-quarter revenue growth of 12.0% year on year, with growth sped up by 11.0 pp from the previous quarter, though TTM revenue growth is only 4.9%. Holding the score back are quality at 44, with an operating margin of -28.6% and an FCF margin of 1.6%, and valuation at 22: in absolute terms P/FCF of 180.1x is high and the FCF yield is 4.4 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, even though the stock is cheap against its own history on P/S (cheaper than at 48 of the last 61 month-ends), with P/FCF and EV/EBIT not comparable.
key_risks: Operating margin of -28.6% and thin free cash flow (1.6% FCF margin) leave little profit support under the share price.
Valuation is high in absolute terms, with P/FCF of 180.1x and an FCF yield 4.4 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield.
Leadership uncertainty after the CEO's August resignation, with law firms soliciting investors for possible securities claims; no suit has been filed so far.
Company guidance called for a low-single-digit organic revenue decline in fiscal Q4, so the 2026-11-10 report could undercut the recent growth acceleration.
After a large run-up the shares sit 16.7% above their 50-day average and near their 52-week high, so a pullback could weaken the trend score.
what_would_change: Up to Buy (9 points needed): a clear move toward operating profitability and stronger free cash flow, which would lift both the quality and valuation scores.
Up: sustained double-digit quarterly revenue growth in the 2026-11-10 report and beyond, which would raise the growth score.
Down to Sell (12 points of cushion): a sharp price reversal that erodes the 87 trend score, combined with growth slipping back toward a decline.
Down: negative news, such as a lawsuit actually being filed or a guidance cut, which would pull the news risk score below its neutral 50.
